decision_basis: Cortistatin-14 activation of human MRGPRX2, structural/ternary receptor evidence, Gi/Gq coupling, and human mast-cell Ca2+/SOCE and degranulation outputs support qualified-high relay/function evidence; mouse MrgprB2 is not substituted for human MRGPRX2.

Cortistatin-14 binding to human SSTR1 and CST17 inhibition of forskolin-stimulated adenylyl cyclase in stably expressing cells support qualified-high receptor-proximal relay evidence; no downstream terminal-TF claim is made.

Cortistatin-14 binding to human SSTR2 and CST17 inhibition of forskolin-stimulated adenylyl cyclase in stably expressing cells support qualified-high receptor-proximal relay evidence; subtype efficacy and coupling remain context-limited.

Cortistatin-14 binding to human SSTR3 and CST17 inhibition of forskolin-stimulated adenylyl cyclase in stably expressing cells support qualified-high receptor-proximal relay evidence; recombinant pharmacology is not native SCI-state evidence.

Cortistatin-14 binding to human SSTR4 and CST17 inhibition of forskolin-stimulated adenylyl cyclase in stably expressing cells support qualified-high receptor-proximal relay evidence; subtype-specific efficacy and coupling remain bounded.

Cortistatin-14 binding to human SSTR5 and CST17 inhibition of forskolin-stimulated adenylyl cyclase in stably expressing cells support qualified-high receptor-proximal relay evidence; no downstream terminal-TF claim is made.

CRH/CRHR1-dependent cAMP/PKA, beta-arrestin/MAPK, ERK/p38, and neuronal or microglial cellular outputs support qualified-high relay/function evidence; CREB and POU6f1 remain measured context-specific readouts, not universal terminal-TF or SCI endpoints.
